text:
maria: FYI we just had a bad regression during the scale-down of the gpu pools. Several jobs OOM'd when pods got rescheduled between MIG and whole-gpu nodepools.
aj: ugh, details? which pools and what triggered the scale-down?
samir: autoscaler triggered a burst scale-down after a traffic dip. It tried to consolidate pods onto fewer nodes and knocked a few MIG-config nodes first.
maria: exactly — we mix A100-MIG nodepool (8g.1) and a whole-gpu pool (a100-40gb). CA picked the smaller MIG nodes to remove and kubelet evicted pods that assumed dedicated whole GPUs. Some pods lost device plugin allocations and failed with OOM.
elaine: do pods use resource requests for fractional GPUs (nvidia.com/gpu: 0.25) or device plugin allocations?
maria: mixed. Most inference pods request fractional GPUs (we let the device plugin expose MIG slices), but a few legacy jobs request full GPUs and tolerate only whole-gpu nodes via nodeAffinity. The autoscaler moved them around during churn.
kyle: two quick mitigations: 1) split nodepools by gpu-sharing mode and mark them with labels (gpu-sharing:mig vs gpu-sharing:whole). 2) set pod nodeAffinity/anti-affinity so fractional pods avoid whole-gpu nodes.
aj: +1 to split. Also set cluster-autoscaler expander to "most-pods" and use scale-down-delay to reduce burst downsizing.
samir: we should also tweak CA's unneeded-time and scale-down-utilization-threshold so it doesn't evict on short traffic blips.
maria: agreed. Another issue: when draining MIG nodes, device-plugin teardown delays cause pods to rebind and request full cuda memory which fails. We need graceful drain + annotated fallback.
elaine: can we add a preStop that gracefully flushes caches and saves KV to redis before eviction? That'd reduce OOM during restart.
kyle: or use pod disruption budgets for critical workers so CA won't evict them in the same cycle.
sre-bot: autoscaler event: scaledDown 3 nodes from pool-gpu-mig-8g. Reason: low utilization.
aj: nice. For a longer-term fix: autoscaler should be aware of GPU packing fragmentation. Maybe a custom CA webhook that evaluates packing score based on requested fractional GPU units.
maria: I sketched a quick nodeSelector + taint plan: label pools and add toleration for mig-only pods, default scheduling to mig pool for fractional requests. Here's a snippet: ```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: inference-x
spec:
  nodeSelector:
    gpu-sharing: "mig"
  tolerations:
  - key: "gpu-mode"
    operator: "Equal"
    value: "mig"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
  resources:
    limits:
      nvidia.com/gpu: "0.25"
```
samir: snippet looks good. Also consider kube-scheduler predicate plugin for topology-aware packing to avoid scattering fractional pods across many nodes.
elaine: question on cost: if we split pools, do we keep same autoscaling params? splitting might increase idle GPUs and cost.
kyle: we'll set smaller min nodes on the MIG pool and a larger buffer on the whole-gpu pool. Plus enable burst autoscale on whole-gpu for sudden heavy full-GPU jobs.
aj: ops runbook: - label pools; - add scale-down-delay 10m; - set max-empty-burst to 1; - add PDBs for critical pods; - rollout in canary region.
maria: I'll open a RFC but we can hotfix by tagging nodes and adding nodeAffinity + increase scale-down delay now.
sre-bot: deploy job queued: apply k8s patch to cluster-autoscaler configmap (scaleDownDelay=600s).
elaine: let's also add alert: high device-plugin teardown time > 30s during node drain. If that fires, we revert scale-down changes.
aj: ordering note: change labels + taints first, then update deployments to use new selectors, then adjust CA. Avoid doing CA change first or we'll get churn.
maria: good call. I'll start on labels/taints AND add a small script to stagger drains (annotation-based) so CA respects a custom drain-backoff annotation.
samir: can you post the script in #eng-infra once ready? I'll test it in staging.
maria: will do. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
